name: Barcelona 2014/15 (Luis Enrique)
scopeNote: Barcelona 2014/15 under Luis Enrique: first competitive match Elche 3-0 (24 Aug 2014, per Wikipedia mirror; the Gamper Trophy 18 Aug is a friendly) to the Champions League final 3-1 Juventus (6 Jun 2015). Style named by sources: base 4-3-3 with a more direct, counter-attacking approach built on the MSN front three (Grantland: 'Tiki-Taka's Trojan Horse'; FourFourTwo: 'more direct, stronger at counter-attacks'); the label 'pure tiki-taka/possession' is wrong for this team (possession fell, long balls rose) though sources still call it possession-based (69% in La Liga per B/R). Mostly tier C/B press analysis; no Coaches' Voice, Spielverlagerung or Zonal Marking piece for 2014/15 was found. Manager-level facts (2015/16 onwards) were not used here. Two entries are verified:false because outside the period (FourFourTwo 2016/17 build-up; 2016 stated-view quote).
openQuestions: Zonal to man-marking at set pieces rests on a single Bleacher Report piece (Nov 2014) plus its Squawka figure (two headed goals conceded); not confirmed by a second source or by the club.
Squad age: only quotes (Nadal: 'the players are older') found; no verified average age or minutes table for Xavi/Iniesta/Alves.

Messi reconciliation: Luis Enrique's 2019 Catalunya Radio quote confirms a 'tiempo de tension' that was 'solved'; no dated primary account of the reconciliation itself was mined. Zubizarreta sacking (5 Jan 2015) seen only in search summaries.
Sportskeeda analysis (Apr 2015) describes a flat 4-4-2 out of possession and a deeper block after 1-0 vs Real Madrid: one match, not a season-long pattern.
Goalkeeper split (Bravo league, Ter Stegen cup/Champions League) seen only in a search summary, not verified.
Pressing: high pressing is described in tier C/B pieces (Sports Mole, Sportskeeda, SI), with no pressing data (PPDA) found.
